Let \(A\) be the origin, and write
\[
x=\overrightarrow{AB},\qquad y=\overrightarrow{AC},\qquad z=\overrightarrow{AD}.
\]
Let
\[
G=(x_i\cdot x_j)_{1\le i,j\le 3},\qquad D=\det G.
\]
Then the tetrahedron volume is
\[
V=\frac{\sqrt D}{6}.
\]

Since
\[
[ABC]=[ABD]=[ACD]=1,
\]
the three \(2\times2\) principal minors of \(G\) are all equal to \(4\). Hence, for \(H=G^{-1}\),
\[
H_{11}=H_{22}=H_{33}=\frac4D.
\]

Now consider the face \(BCD\). Let \(e=(1,1,1)^T\). The plane through \(x,y,z\) has normal proportional to \(X^{-T}e\), so
\[
4[BCD]^2=D\, e^T G^{-1}e.
\]
Thus
\[
D\,e^THe=4s^2.
\]

Define
\[
K=\frac D4 H.
\]
Then \(K\) is positive definite, has diagonal entries \(1\), and satisfies
\[
e^TKe=s^2.
\]
Also
\[
\det K=\left(\frac D4\right)^3\det H=\frac{D^2}{64}.
\]
So maximizing volume is equivalent to maximizing \(\det K\).

Write \(u=e/\sqrt3\). In an orthonormal basis beginning with \(u\),
\[
K=\begin{pmatrix}
a & b^T\\
b & C
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad a=u^TKu=\frac{s^2}{3}.
\]
Since \(\operatorname{tr}K=3\), we have \(\operatorname{tr}C=3-a\). By the Schur complement,
\[
\det K=a\det\left(C-\frac{bb^T}{a}\right).
\]
For a positive semidefinite \(2\times2\) matrix with trace \(T\), the determinant is at most \(T^2/4\). Hence
\[
\det K\le a\left(\frac{3-a}{2}\right)^2
=\frac{s^2(9-s^2)^2}{108}.
\]
Equality holds exactly when \(b=0\) and \(C=\frac{3-a}{2}I\). Therefore every maximizer has
\[
K_*=\begin{pmatrix}
1&c&c\\
c&1&c\\
c&c&1
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
c=\frac{s^2-3}{6}.
\]
Thus all maximizers have the same Gram matrix up to orthogonal motion, hence the same circumradius.

At equality,
\[
D^2=64\det K_*=\frac{16}{27}s^2(9-s^2)^2,
\]
so
\[
D=\frac{4s(9-s^2)}{3\sqrt3}.
\]
Since
\[
G=\frac D4 K_*^{-1},
\]
and \(K_*\) has eigenvalues
\[
\frac{s^2}{3},\qquad \frac{9-s^2}{6},\qquad \frac{9-s^2}{6},
\]
one gets
\[
(G_{11},G_{22},G_{33})=
\frac{s^2+3}{\sqrt3\,s}.
\]
Let \(O\) be the circumcenter relative to \(A=0\). It satisfies
\[
x\cdot O=y\cdot O=z\cdot O=\frac{G_{11}}2.
\]
Therefore
\[
R^2=|O|^2
=\frac14 d^TG^{-1}d,
\]
where \(d=(G_{11},G_{22},G_{33})^T\). Using \(e^TG^{-1}e=4s^2/D\), this gives
\[
R^2=\frac{\sqrt3\,(s^2+3)^2}{4s(9-s^2)}.
\]

Hence the common circumradius is
\[
\boxed{R(s)=\frac{3^{1/4}(s^2+3)}{2\sqrt{s(9-s^2)}}}.
\]
